reason: source exceeded lean-ctx per-file search cap, so ctx_search skipped it silently (docs/AGENT_ENVIRONMENT.md addendum H fact 1)
policy: verbatim contiguous line ranges; original order preserved; no text reformatted, reordered or edited

ranges.disposition: replaced by the new header/index block in docs/currentstate.md

verification.method: reconstruct from disk in ORIGINAL ORDER - preamble kept in the source (19 B) + recent entries kept in the source + each shard read back with its 8-line header stripped + the tail kept in the source - and compare sha256 AND byte count against the original working-tree file
verification.shard_bodies: each shard body compared against its declared source line range AND its trailing CRLF - all five EXACT
how_this_check_failed_before_it_passed: attempt 1 (in-memory, during the split): PASSED, and is what licensed writing the files
attempt 2 (from disk): reported FAIL because it omitted the recent-entries range (source lines 3..43, kept in the active file) - artifact correct, check wrong

attempt 3 (from disk): reported FAIL twice over - the split had introduced a stray blank line after the recent-entries heading (+2 B), and the check concatenated the kept pieces AFTER the shards instead of in original order; the stray blank was removed and the order fixed
lesson recorded because it matters: a from-disk proof catches integration mistakes the in-memory proof cannot, and a length-preserving reordering is only detectable by the hash
verification.caveat_for_later_verification: git show HEAD:docs/currentstate.md returns the LF-normalised blob (550,051 B), NOT the CRLF working-tree bytes, because core.autocrlf=true; a verbatim re-check must use the sha256 recorded here (or convert the blob to CRLF first, which reproduces the original exactly - verified).
